q-111763.name: Question 1
q-111763.problem:
Consider the standard matrices of three linear transformations shown below. Which of the transformations map ${R}^{2}$ onto a line?

$$
{T}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 9\end{aligned}],\,{T}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{T}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 9 \\ 6 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
q-111763.worked_solution:
Given a linear transformation over ${R}^{2}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ we have the following:

- $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto ${R}^{2}$ if and only if $\text{rank}(T)=2,$ i.e., $T$ is nonsingular.

- $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line if and only if $\text{rank}(T)=1.$

- $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto $(0,0)$ if and only if $\text{rank}(T)=0,$ i.e., $T$ is the zero matrix.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- ${T}_{1}$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line. Notice that the columns of ${T}_{1}$ are linearly dependent but it's not the zero matrix. So, $\text{rank}({T}_{1})=1.$

- ${T}_{2}$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto $(0,0)$ since ${T}_{2}$ is the zero matrix, i.e. $\text{rank}({T}_{2})=0.$

- ${T}_{3}$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto ${R}^{2}.$ Indeed, ${T}_{3}$ is a nonsingular matrix, i.e. $\text{rank}({T}_{3})=2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{1}$ only."

q-38297.name: Question 8
q-38297.problem:
Consider a linear transformation $T$ that maps ${R}^{2}$ to the origin. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{rank}(T)=1$,  where $T$ is the standard matrix of $T$

II. $\text{Im}(T)$ contains no vectors of ${R}^{2}$

III. $\text{Ker}(T)={R}^{2}$
q-38297.worked_solution:
Recall that when the image of a linear transformation $T$ in ${R}^{2}$ with the standard matrix $T$ is the zero-subspace $\{0\},$ then

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=0
$$

and, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T) & =2-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =2-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is false. In our case, we have 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=0.
$$

- Statement II is false. The image of $T$ contains the vector zero vector $0=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, the condition $\text{nullity}(T)=2$ in ${R}^{2}$ is equivalent to 

$$
\text{Ker}(T)={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

If $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto the line $5y=6x$ then, which of the following statements are true?

II. $\text{Ker}(T)\ne \{0\}$

III. $\text{nullity}(T)=0$, where $T$ is the standard matrix of $T$

Recall that when the image of a linear transformation $T$ in ${R}^{2}$ with the standard matrix $T$ is a one-dimensional line, then

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=1
$$

and, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T) & =2-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =2-1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

Since $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line passing through the origin, we have that the standard matrix $T$ is singular. So, $\text{Ker}(T)\ne \{0\}.$

- Statement III is false.
Since  statement II is true we have that $\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim(Ker}(T))\ne 0.$
